title: Bunker test plane for mischief's own development: agent at tick start, evidence pulled back, agent destroyed, zero main-host residue
reasoning:
The busted assumption worth naming: a foreman lane runs its commands on the host the scheduler lives on. For every other project that is fine — they build and test their own code. For a fault injector it is not fine, because the work IS the fault, and the worker's own cwd sits next to the scheduler, the gateway and the memory daemon.

So mischief's lane needs a TEST PLANE, not a promise:
  - every tick that exercises a primitive runs on an ephemeral bunker agent
  - the agent is created at tick start and destroyed at tick end (or on a bounded TTL, whichever is shorter)
  - nothing lands on the main host: no scratch dirs, no armed faults, no leftover agents
  - the evidence (journal + the landed-proof counters) is PULLED BACK before destroy, so the tick's report is produced from artifacts, not from the agent's memory
  - an agent that cannot be obtained is a recorded SKIP with a named reason, never a silent pass — the fleet has a fresh precedent for why (a QA lane reported a full battery from an agent that had already been destroyed)

WHAT TO REUSE, NOT REBUILD: the fleet already has three working planes. bunker-qa.sh (one-shot battery, JIT agent, toolchain bootstrap, collect, destroy), bunker-soak.sh (long-duration soak with a fault ladder and a verdict engine), and gauntlet (~/gauntlet — the standalone Go fault battery with 16 cells and a jolt relay, proven against trouble on a scratch port with no bunker). This row is the integration, and its first job is to decide which of the three is the substrate rather than inventing a fourth.

THE HARD PART, stated so it is not discovered mid-build: `mischief`'s L0/L1 primitives (signals, systemd-run --user scopes, the LD_PRELOAD shim, the seccomp supervisor, the userspace proxy) are exactly the set a bunker agent CAN run — measured, the shim and user-scope limits work rootless. The L2/L3 set (netns+netem, dm/loop, freezer, docker) cannot, so those need either a sanctioned non-fleet box or a container with NET_ADMIN, and the spec must say which. Do not let the plane's convenience silently shrink the catalogue: name the primitives the plane cannot exercise and file that as its own gap.
acceptance_criteria: AC: (1) One command takes a clean sanctioned host from nothing to evidence: obtain agent -> ship repo -> build (no `make` dependency on a bare agent; it has no C toolchain) -> run the L0/L1 selftest -> pull the journal and the landed-proof counters back -> destroy the agent. (2) After it returns, the main host shows NO residue: no scratch state, no armed faults, no surviving agent, and the evidence is present locally. (3) An unobtainable agent is reported as a recorded SKIP with a named reason and is never rendered as a pass. (4) The set of primitives the plane CANNOT exercise (the L2/L3 set needing privileges a bunker agent lacks) is enumerated in the spec with the sanctioned environment for each, not left implied. Evidence: one full transcript plus the main-host residue check before/after.

Scheduler readiness: register the project, then the satellites — with the isolation constraint attached to the lane itself.

WHAT "READY FOR THE SCHEDULER" ACTUALLY REQUIRES (derived, not guessed):

 - ONE enabled lane per workdir (the API 409s a second, case-insensitively). `<workdir>` is free today; verify before registering rather than after.
 - `namespace_id`, `deliver` and the model/provider pair, matching the fleet's convention. `mischief`'s the knowledge store namespace now exists (created 2026-09-28), so `namespace_id` has something real to point at.

 - the lane's consumers read `status == "pending"` and nothing else. Every row filed for this project must land pending; a row left in any other spelling is invisible to the foreman. This is measured, not asserted: the scheduler's own board_awareness counts only pending, and the fleet gate's allowed set is (pending, in_progress, complete, duplicate).

THE SATELLITE SET — derive it from the fleet's convention rather than inventing it: a primary plus the standard satellites (`-qa`, `-sync`, `-pm`, `-docs`, `-releng`, `-review`), each in its OWN namespace, all reading the primary's board. The one that is genuinely distinctive here is the CHAOS/BATTERY satellite: it runs the project's fault matrix on a cadence and files findings, and it is the satellite that makes this project self-testing. It is also the satellite with the highest blast radius, so it inherits MSF-020's isolation contract in full — it may not run a fault on the scheduler's own host.

The lane should exist EARLY and run a deliberately tiny matrix (the primitives that already work rootless on a scratch target), because a lane that only ever runs after the build is finished has never been exercised as a lane — and the fleet's standing lesson is that a pipeline is proven by its destination, not by its configuration.

(2) The primary lane dispatches, reads .coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl, and moves a pending row to in_progress and back — proven by a real tick, not by configuration. (3) The satellite set is derived from the DB (`projects WHERE name LIKE 'mischief%'` plus their workdirs), not hand-listed, and each satellite reads the primary's board. (4) The battery/chaos satellite runs a deliberately tiny matrix against a scratch target and files at least one real finding. (5) No lane in the project runs a fault on the scheduler's own host — verified by the isolation check of MSF-020, not by inspection of intent.

title: P1 — TestOwnerSurvivesKill9AndRevertsAtTTL fails on ANY clean machine: systemd-run --user owner unit dies 203/EXEC inside a private /tmp mount namespace (bunker/pam_namespace), CLI reads success while the TTL owner is already dead

Every other package ok. DEV-BOX CONTRAST: the same test at the same HEAD is green on the dev box (go1.26.9) — and on the agent with MISCHIEF_REVERTER_DETACH_MODE=setsid — so the defect is the systemd-run detach shape, not the reverter logic. Reproduced on the agent directly: systemd-run --user --collect -p RuntimeMaxSec=N <binary> __owner ... returns rc=0, but journalctl shows the unit 'Main process exited, code=exited, status=203/EXEC' within the same second — /run/user/<uid>/systemd exists so systemdUserReachable() picks systemd-run, but the USER MANAGER runs OUTSIDE the agent's per-session pam_namespace /tmp mount namespace and cannot exec the CLI binary (or see any /tmp paths). The CLI sees systemd-run rc=0 and records mode=systemd-run as success; the owner is dead before the fault lands; the TTL revert never happens. This is exactly the failure mode the test exists to catch (AC-5: CLI kill -9 mid-hold still reverts at TTL) — on any host with private-tmp user managers (bunker, containers, hardened multi-tenant boxes) the product silently loses EVERY TTL revert. detail.evidence: internal/daemon/daemon.go:51-52 documents the field as 'DaemonBoot is the daemon's own boot id (reverter fold identity)' and render() sets it from st.BootID (:182). title: P2 — lifecycle ops are not atomic: a failed `uninstall` has already deleted the helper manifest (runs + prefix left behind, rc=1, no per-step report), and an unprivileged `install` mkdirs the prefix before the privilege refusal it had already predicted

detail.evidence: Same run as MISCHIEF-DF-33 (HEAD f7f29be / product 1b53e52). (1) UNINSTALL: after the DF-33 abort, `find /tmp/df-mc-r16/p4` returns ONLY `/tmp/df-mc-r16/p4` — helper-manifest.json is GONE, the run dirs are untouched, rc=1; the successful path prints a `removed <path>` line per step (rc=0, `uninstall: 4 artefact(s) removed`) while the failing run prints NO step lines, so the removals execute before the abort line the user sees. On a host with the drop-in present the plan order is drop-in -> manifest -> run dirs, i.e. a failed `mischief uninstall --keep-days N` tears down the privileged surface and then reports only a failure. (2) INSTALL (mirror case, same non-atomicity): `mischief install --prefix /tmp/df-mc-r16/p2` unprivileged prints the advisory `ADVISORY: /etc/sudoers.d/mischief requires root (sudo install) — an unprivileged prefix (/tmp/df-mc-r16/p2) cannot carry /etc/sudoers.d/mischief`, then attempts that exact write anyway: `install: install: write /etc/sudoers.d/mischief: open /etc/sudoers.d/mischief: permission denied` rc=1, and leaves the freshly `mkdir`ed empty prefix `/tmp/df-mc-r16/p2` behind (mkdir is plan action 1, the privileged write is action 2). Fix direction: pre-flight the WHOLE plan before executing any step (including whether the rotation's targets are removable), or keep executing but report per-step status and leave a resumable record; for install, screen the known-impossible privileged action before the mkdir (the advisory already knows the answer) or clean up on refusal. reasoning:
Dogfood run 2026-10-18 06:48Z (lane mischief-chaos-dogfood), clean-HEAD export of HEAD 2d1ed37b5cdf5c638525b4056b80b29232c4afd9, bin 2d1ed37b5cdf, live legs on ephemeral sanctioned bunker agent f306b7bd.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGH-VALUE SURFACE: every prior dogfood tick drove `battery --quick`; the FULL-matrix + FILING path (`--project`, `--primitive`, `--out`, `--file-rows`) that docs/CHAOS-LANE.md §6 step 3 names as the chaos lane's tick body and docs/BATTERY-PARITY.md §'Replacement command line' names as the shipped replacement had never been driven (grep of the whole dogfood log: zero hits for `file-rows`, `battery --project`).

WHAT WAS DRIVEN (all rc=0, artefacts inspected): `battery --project mischief --file-rows` 11 cells 5 pass / 6 named skips / 0 fail, run 2f5f4eef999c04c9, journal landed=5 reverted=5, matrix.json/matrix.md + findings.jsonl written; `--primitive N-012 --file-rows` (the documented release-gate cell) run fedb6e7e59fd9979; `--quick --file-rows` run aaf4de007edb5f29; `--dry-run --project mischief` 11 cells. The surface WORKS; the defect is in the row ids it emits.

EVIDENCE — TEMPLATE (battery): internal/battery/runner.go:236 mints `ID: fmt.Sprintf("MSF-BAT-%s", c.Cell.ID)` and the cell ids this run OBSERVED are the project-scoped form `mischief/F-009`, `mischief/N-012`, ... (printed by `battery --dry-run --project mischief` and carried in matrix.json as `cell_id`). So the emitted id is `MSF-BAT-mischief/F-009` — a slash and lowercase letters, neither of which the fleet id law allows. The adverse branch that actually writes such a row is NOT reachable on a healthy host (see the log's coverage note), so this half is template+observed-input, not a captured emission.

EVIDENCE — LIVE (chaos finding): `mischief chaos finding --project mischief --board <scratch board> --title 'battery finding: F-009 on mischief (not_recovered) - probe' --reason ... --priority P1 --primitive F-009` -> rc=0, stdout `chaos finding: MSF-CHAOS-2dfb1056d701 filed ... (1 row)`; the appended row is verbatim: {"id":"MSF-CHAOS-2dfb1056d701","status":"pending",...}. That id is content-addressed (docs/CHAOS-LANE.md §5 MSF-CHAOS-<hex(sha256)[:12]>) and the hex is LOWERCASE.

EVIDENCE — THE REFUSAL (fleet tooling, same boardctl the repo's own pre-commit board-lint installs):
  boardctl update -C <scratch> "MSF-BAT-mischief/F-009" --status complete --note ...   -> rc=1
    boardctl: task id "MSF-BAT-mischief/F-009" does not match the fleet id format ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)+$ ... (pass --force to write it anyway)
  boardctl create -C <scratch> --id "MSF-BAT-mischief/C-009" --title ...            -> rc=1 (same)
  boardctl update -C <scratch> "MSF-CHAOS-2dfb1056d701" --status complete --note ... -> rc=1 (same)
  CONTROL (legal id, same board): boardctl update "MSF-BAT-MISCHIEF-F-009" --status complete -> rc=0 'updated task ...'.
  boardctl validate -C <scratch> --fail-on dangling-dep on BOTH boards -> rc=0 'RESULT: OK (1 warning(s))' (warnings are about the non-canon project/primitive/verdict/reason keys, not the id).

IMPACT: the lane's whole promise is 'findings without an operator' (MSF-017). The operator-free loop files a row, the primary's board scan dispatches it, and the row can never be closed or edited without --force; a re-file of the same finding is refused by boardctl create on the same grounds. It slips through review because the AC-18 criterion named boardctl VALIDATE (MSF-011 acceptance_criteria: 'AC-18 (rows land on the owning board, boardctl validate clean)') and validate has no id-format check — the one command that enforces the law is create/update.

FIX DIRECTION: mint ids the law accepts (e.g. sanitize the cell id: `MSF-BAT-<PROJECT>-<PRIM>-<run8>`, uppercase hex for the chaos hash), and add the fleet id regex to battery.ValidateRows so the emit path refuses its own malformed row before it reaches a board (the validator already refuses a missing id / bad status / bad verdict; the format is the gap).

title: P4 — no per-cell timing survives any battery artefact: all 13 journal records of an 11-cell run carry the same 1-second-resolution ts and no record type has a duration field, the CLI prints verdicts without times and the matrix artefact has no timing column — so an operator cannot answer 'which cell is slow / how long did the fault hold' from the record. (No PERF row filed: nothing measured is user-noticeable — full matrix 0.911s cold / 0.816s warm, --quick 0.586s, N-012 alone 0.028s, dry-run 0.018-0.028s.)
reasoning:
Dogfood run 2026-10-18 06:48Z (Step 2b performance leg), clean-HEAD bin 2d1ed37b5cdf on ephemeral sanctioned agent f306b7bd.

MEASURED (wall clock, this run, 8-vCPU agent, loadavg 1.41): full matrix + filing `battery --project mischief --file-rows` 911ms cold (run 2f5f4eef999c04c9) and 816ms warm (run 31b2dc9074d1c370); `--quick --file-rows` 586ms (aaf4de007edb5f29); release-gate cell `--primitive N-012` 28ms (fedb6e7e59fd9979); `--dry-run --project mischief` 18-28ms over 10 warm runs (mean 21.7ms); `--quick --dry-run` 20-27ms over 5. NOTHING here is slow enough for a user to notice, and this row is deliberately NOT a perf claim — no PERF row exists for this surface because a win nobody can feel is not a finding.

THE GAP: while measuring, the question 'where did the 911ms go' was unanswerable from the product's own records. Pulled journal (run-full/battery.jsonl, 3768 bytes, sha-verified through the plane's collect leg style): 13 records — 1 run_planned, 5 fault_landed, 5 fault_reverted, 1 verdict, 1 run_closed — and EVERY record carries `ts: 1792306814` (identical, because the whole 0.911s run sits inside one second) with no duration/elapsed field on any type (keys are exactly: type, run_id, seq, ts, fields). The CLI's per-cell lines print verdict + reason only, the summary prints counts, and matrix.json/matrix.md carry verdict/detection/recovery with no timing. So neither the artefact nor the journal can answer per-cell land time, hold time or revert time; a flaky cell that takes 30s of a 31s run is invisible, and SPEC-05's detection-window measurement (DetectionEntry.Within, the land-to-detect duration) has no comparable per-cell number to sit beside.

FIX DIRECTION: stamp per-cell millisecond marks into the journal records (plan/land/proof/revert) and echo them in the CLI summary + matrix artefact; the field vocabulary already reserves a Within duration on the detection side, and the SPEC-02 journal schema is the owner of the record shape.

detail.evidence: pulled run-full/battery.jsonl (13 records, ts=1792306814 on all, no duration field); live wall-clock timings above; matrix.json/matrix.md have no timing column.

reasoning: Found by the foreman during wave mischief-foreman-2026-10-19-22-15-21 while grading the three merged rows. The gitreins tier-1 'tests' step for MISCHIEF-DF-47 (verdict 04d44487, commit 73be820) reported `--- FAIL: TestArmRefusesUnsanctionedHost (0.01s)  arm_test.go:78: arm on unsanctioned host: exit 0, want 2`, while the same suite was green on the same tree in the foreman's own gate and green in CI. So the test is environment-dependent: it exercises the fail-closed sanction refusal but does not clear MISCHIEF_SANCTION/MISCHIEF_SANCTION_FILE from its own environment, so any runner that exports the sanction (the repo's own workflows export MISCHIEF_SANCTION=1 for the selftest and battery steps, and a harness may inherit it) reports a phantom red on an unchanged tree. Fix direction: make the test self-contained - unset/clear the sanction env in the test process (t.Setenv("MISCHIEF_SANCTION", "") plus an explicit unset path) instead of relying on the caller's environment, and assert both arms (unset -> exit 2, set -> exit 0) so the refusal contract is proven rather than inherited. Not a code regression: arm's refusal behaviour is unchanged.

  Controls, same minute: bare `mischief plan -f catalog/experiments/ex-001-noop-detector.yaml` -> rc=2 host_not_sanctioned; `env -u MISCHIEF_SANCTION mischief status --dir <D>` rc=1; arm/selftest/battery all refuse unsanctioned (sanction.Check wired there).

CODE CENSUS (file:line): sanction.Check is called in exactly four verb paths — cmd/mischief/plan.go:76, cmd/mischief/selftest.go:54, cmd/mischief/battery.go:75, cmd/mischief/arm.go:130 (plus the doctor seam internal/doctor/checks.go:20 and the lane-template check internal/chaos/lane.go:297 which only validates that a TEMPLATE declares Sanctioned:true — its own comment says 'the runtime enforces the real marker (sanction.Check) before any landing act', which for the sim verb is false). cmd/mischief/sim.go imports neither internal/sanction nor internal/rails; cmdChaosMatrix (cmd/mischief/chaos.go:65) likewise checks nothing host-level. The PRD's rule (docs/prd/mischief-v0.1.md:255-263): 'A host admits mischief only when it carries an explicit sanction marker (file + env). Absence is a REFUSAL with a non-zero exit, not a warning — fail closed.' The M1a acceptance (PRD:363) says the gate is 'enforced, with a test that fails if the marker check is neutered'. The help line (cmd/mischief/main.go:165) still claims 'sanction-marker gate (SPEC-13) fail-closed' as a blanket.

WHY THIS IS A FINDING RATHER THAN DESIGN: (1) sim ARMS a fault shape and LANDS a request against it — that is a landing act by the product's own vocabulary (its output says 'landed in the simulator' with the request log as landed proof), and the sim process binds a port and writes durable artifacts on the host; (2) the sim surface is reachable WITHOUT any sanction env on the fleet's main protected host, which is exactly the scenario SPEC-13/MSF-020 exists for ('a fault injector pointed at it by accident is not a bug, it is an outage'); (3) MSF-032 already established the class — selftest/battery were gated for precisely this reason and the fix comment (cmd/mischief/main.go:26-27) says 'the sanction marker gate runs before any verb that could arm or land', but sim (and chaos) were missed; (4) the two pending rows MISCHIEF-DF-28-R2/DF-65 cover the LOAD gate's absence on the same verbs — the sanction gate is a separate rail with the same gap, and neither row claims it.

That still violates the PRD's fail-closed sentence verbatim ('a host ADMITS mischief only when...' — sim admits), and an unsanctioned host is supposed to refuse every verb that exercises a primitive. If the maintainers intend sim to be exempt (sandbox-by-construction), the exemption must be written (help line + sim --help + TEST-PLANE) like the load-gate exemption DF-65 asks for.

On HEAD 9abe981: `mischief status` shows 'holds: 1 ... stuck ... ttl_remaining=-185h37m15s' (target file long since deleted from tmpfs — the fault is not live, yet every surface reports a live-ish hold); `mischief revert --all` prints 'reverted b7e9f744dfb5a67d outcome=revert_failed ... inverse kind "restore_file": unknown (refusing to execute)', summary '0 holds reverted, 1 revert_failed', stderr 'kill switch sweep did not fully revert — at least one fault may still be live', rc=1; afterwards the hold folds to terminal revert_failed (holds: 0) — the exit path is honest but the fault fact is permanently unresolvable. ROOT CAUSE: git log -S shows the spelling restore_file NEVER existed in internal/reverter source; the whitelist (MISCHIEF-DF-29 3cc92be, DF-29-R2 4dc6cfc) is hyphenated (restore-file, remove-file; checks file-matches-backup, file-absent; record.go:101-104). The documented flagship loop worked end to end: `arm --fault S-001 --target scratch:W --ttl 30s --inverse-kind restore-file --inverse-params path=W/config.toml,backup=W/config.toml.bak --check-kind file-matches-backup ...` rc=0, manual LAND (`printf FAULTED > config.toml`), `serve --dir RUN` reverted the hold at TTL (proof ts 1793139814 vs expiry 1793139813, i.e. +1s at the 1s poll cadence, inverse duration 177.74us) and restored the file to `original`. A hold that expired WHILE NO daemon was running (W6, ttl_remaining=-33s, target still FAULTED) was reverted by boot reconcile on the next `serve` start (proof own_pid=3302962, file back to `orig6`). The documented recovery table also held: plain `revert --hold <id>` on a terminal revert_failed hold refused rc=1 with the --retry pointer; `--retry` with the cause still broken measured revert_failed again rc=1; after healing (chmod 644 on the backup) `--retry` measured `reverted` rc=0 and the target matched the backup; `status` exit 1 + `revert_failed: 1` counter and health.json `ok:false` agreed. THE DEFECT: `serve` has no single-owner guard on a run dir, and nothing in the docs claims one. A second `mischief serve --dir RUN` started while pid 3147786 was already live on that dir (the background wrapper for the first daemon) came up normally, printed its banner and kept running -- no refusal, no warning, rc=124 only because the harness bounded it. Its child was pid 3208558. Immediately afterwards health.json's `pid` was 3208558 (generated_at 1793139970) while the hold armed at ts 1793139952 (bf4a22b73b389339, ttl 15s) was reverted at ts 1793139969 by own_pid=3147786 -- the FIRST daemon. So the one ownership signal the product publishes, health.json's `pid`, last-writer-wins between two live daemons and can name a process that did not perform the revert. Operational consequence: an operator or supervisor that treats health.json's `pid` as 'the watchdog' reads and signals the wrong process; killing it leaves the other daemon reverting TTLs, so 'the watchdog is stopped' can be false, and no surface reports that a duplicate daemon owns the dir. HONEST LIMIT: no double revert was observed in this window -- each hold got exactly one ttl_expiry revert_proof row (one daemon folded the other's terminal proof), so the duplicate-race hazard is plausible but NOT demonstrated here; only the identity/last-writer ownership is proven. Reproduce: start serve A on RUN, start serve B on the same RUN, arm a hold with --ttl 15s, land the fault, then compare `jq .pid RUN/health.json` against `own_pid` in RUN/reverter.jsonl. Evidence: /tmp/mc-df-20261027-2221/run/reverter.jsonl, .../run/health.json, .../serve.out, .../serve2.out. acceptance_criteria: 1) A second `mischief serve --dir D` started while another serve already owns D either refuses with the product's uniform named-refusal contract (nonzero exit, reason on stderr, no new daemon loop) or health.json gains an explicit ownership surface that lists every live daemon on D; in either design the `pid` field must never name a process other than the one that wrote that file. 2) The chosen behaviour is pinned by a regression test under internal/daemon/ (and internal/reverter/ where the store is involved). 3) The duplicate-daemon hazard is covered by a test asserting that two folds over the same journal produce exactly one revert attempt per hold (no duplicate inverse execution, no duplicate revert_proof row for one hold_id).
acceptance: PASS: mkdir -p /tmp/df71-run /tmp/df71-home && export HOME=/tmp/df71-home MISCHIEF_SANCTION=1 MISCHIEF_SANCTION_FILE=/tmp/df71-sanction; start `bin/mischief serve --dir /tmp/df71-run` in a tracked background terminal (record the child pid via `pgrep -P <wrapper>`), then start a SECOND `bin/mischief serve --dir /tmp/df71-run` in a second tracked terminal. Exactly one of the two behaviours must hold and be observable: (a) the second daemon exits nonzero with a reason naming the owning process, or (b) both run AND `jq -r .pid /tmp/df71-run/health.json` names a pid that is one of the two live daemons AND equals the pid whose revert_proof rows carry the newest ts. In either case arm one hold (`--fault S-001 --ttl 15s --inverse-kind restore-file ...`) and land it, then assert `grep -c '"type":"revert_proof"' /tmp/df71-run/reverter.jsonl` counts exactly one proof for that hold_id. Also run `go test ./internal/daemon/ -count=1` and `go test ./internal/reverter/ -count=1` and require PASS, citing the new test name that pins the chosen behaviour in the commit message.

title: P4 — `version` silently accepts any argument (`--json`, `--nope`, `--help`, a junk word) and exits 0 with the plain string, so a scripted `mischief version --json` gets non-JSON under a success code
reasoning: Real use on HEAD 5ecc160 (detached worktree build, isolated HOME). Every other shipped verb rejects an unknown flag with the uniform Go-flag refusal: `revert --all --json` -> rc=2 `flag provided but not defined: -json`, `retention --dry-run --json` -> rc=2, `battery/sim --json` -> rc=2, and an unknown VERB is refused too (`mischief statu` -> rc=2 `mischief: unknown verb "statu"`; `mischief reverts` -> rc=2), as is a malformed value (`--ttl 30` -> rc=2 `invalid value "30" for flag -ttl: parse error`). `version` is the exception: `mischief version --json`, `version --nope`, `version -h`, `version --help` and `version junk` ALL returned rc=0 and printed the identical plain line `mischief 5ecc160e7fb4`; every argument is swallowed, including the two that conventionally mean 'tell me the flags' and 'machine-readable output'. A user or script doing `mischief version --json | jq -r .version` therefore sees the CLI succeed (rc=0) while the pipe consumes no JSON at all, and a typo'd argument on this verb is invisible. Adjacent, same surface: the built-in usage banner printed by bare `mischief` (which is THE help, since every subcommand's conventional --help exits 2 per the open MISCHIEF-CLI-001) lists `[--json]` for plan, doctor and audit but not for status, whose line reads `mischief status [--dir D] [--all]` -- while PRD 6.1 documents the shipped verb as `mischief status [--all] [--dir D] [--json]` and the flag works (`status --json` emits a pure JSON object, `status --json --dir <absent>` emits `{"run_dir": ..., "state": "absent"}` rc=1). The usage banner is the only place a user looks for the flag; the PRD is not shipped to them. Verified as NOT defects in the same sweep (so they are deliberately not filed): stdout purity -- `plan --json`, `status --json`, `doctor --json`, `audit --json` are all single parseable JSON documents with no trailing human summary, and `plan --json --journal-dir D` keeps the JSON on stdout and puts the journal pointer line on STDERR (jq -e passes on all four); the snake_case key surface of status --json matches the PRD after MISCHIEF-DF-53.
